climate_pressure: Flood and other climate hazards creating displacement risk.
documented_impact: Loss of housing/livelihood stability and disruption of social/economic/legal protections.
fcv_mediator: Recognition, service access and protection gaps can limit safe coping and fair allocation during displacement.
possible_consequence: The ISIS authors warn of escalating resource competition and tensions with host communities or the state; no measured violence outcome.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing inequality, tenure rules, service investment, urban development and wider political/economic conditions also affect displacement and social relations.
uncertainty: Conditional national policy analysis, not local incident evidence or causal evaluation. Legal-protection claims are attributed to the authors, not current legal advice; no displaced-group threat label. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The CCDR recommends targeted housing/livelihood/financial support and inclusive planning; delivery and peace effects are not established.
compact_statement: The 2026 ISIS note warns that climate-related displacement can weaken protective systems and, where recognition/services are inadequate, aggravate resource tensions; this is conditional policy analysis, not observed climate-caused violence.
